value.lineage: Souffle (2016-, Oracle Labs / Sydney): a high-performance Datalog -- bottom-up semi-naive evaluation with a specialised data-structure back end, compiled to parallel C++; the modern engine behind large-scale static program analyses

value.built_to: evaluate Datalog -- compute the least fixpoint of a set of recursive Horn rules over relations -- fast enough for whole-program static analysis of millions of tuples
value.pressure: the semi-naive fixpoint must not recompute derived tuples, and the join/index choices decide whether a real analysis finishes in seconds or hours

cut.note: bottom-up Datalog evaluated semi-naively and compiled: rules are stratified into strongly-connected components evaluated in dependency order; within a recursive component each relation keeps a main store, a delta of the tuples derived in the last round, and a new store for this round; each iteration derives only tuples that use at least one delta tuple (so no derivation is repeated), merges new into main and swaps new into delta, and stops when the delta is empty; the relations are specialised in-memory index structures (B-tree, Brie trie, equivalence-relation) chosen per relation, and the whole thing is either interpreted over a RAM IR or compiled to parallel C++

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: generateRecursiveStratum (303-360): per relation a delta, new and reject store; clear delta; derive clause versions; MergeRelationsWithFilter new -> delta minus reject; clear new; Loop with an Exit on empty delta; generateStratumPreamble/Postamble (454-490) seed and clear the deltas
organs.mechanism: for a recursive component, each relation R has R (all tuples so far), delta-R (tuples new in the previous round) and new-R (tuples derived this round); a round evaluates each recursive rule once per body atom that ranges over the SCC, forcing that atom to read delta while the others read the main relations (the 'delta version' of the clause), so every derived tuple depends on at least one just-derived tuple and nothing is re-derived; new-R minus the existing tuples becomes the next delta, new-R is merged into R, and the loop exits when every delta is empty (the least fixed point is reached)
organs.input: a stratified set of rules and the base facts
assumptions: Datalog's monotone rules have a least fixed point reachable bottom-up; restricting each round to delta-touching derivations avoids the naive method's repeated work (Balbin & Ramamohanarao 1987)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: each derivation done once; the standard efficient Datalog evaluation, the base of large-scale static analysis (Doop, ...)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: stratification must be possible (no recursion through negation or aggregation); the delta/new/reject bookkeeping is intricate and the subsumptive-clause path adds delete relations
organs.human_prior: Balbin & Ramamohanarao 1987 (semi-naive); Bancilhon & Ramakrishnan 1986; Souffle (Scholz et al. 2016)

organs.human_name: generateStratum (161-196): if the SCC is recursive call generateRecursiveStratum else evaluate the single relation once; generateClearExpiredRelations (196); the SCC ordering from the precedence graph
organs.mechanism: the predicate dependency graph is decomposed into strongly-connected components; a component with no internal recursion is evaluated in one pass, a recursive one by the semi-naive loop; components are run in topological order so a relation's dependencies are complete before it is computed; a relation is cleared once no later stratum needs it, bounding memory
assumptions: the program stratifies (negation and aggregation only across component boundaries); computing in dependency order is both correct and memory-bounded
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: large programs evaluated with only the currently-needed relations resident
organs.human_prior: stratified Datalog (Apt, Blair, Walker 1988); the SCC schedule is standard

organs.human_name: src/ram operations (IndexScan, ExistenceCheck, Insert, Loop, Swap, MergeExtend); src/interpreter indexes (BTreeIndex, BrieIndex, EqrelIndex, ProvenanceIndex); the ast2ram -> ram -> interpreter/synthesiser pipeline
organs.mechanism: the semi-naive schedule is emitted as a RAM (relational algebra machine) program of loops, index scans, existence checks and inserts; each relation is backed by a data structure chosen for its access pattern -- a concurrent B-tree for general relations, a Brie (a trie specialised for dense integer tuples), or an equivalence-relation structure for transitive symmetric relations -- and the RAM program is either walked by an interpreter or synthesised to parallel C++ and compiled, so the same evaluation runs interpreted for quick turnaround or compiled for speed
organs.input: the RAM program and the relations
assumptions: the access pattern of each relation is known at compile time, so a specialised index beats a general one; a RAM IR decouples the evaluation strategy from the execution mode
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: Datalog at C++ speed on billions of tuples (the record: the engine behind large-scale static analysis)
organs.human_prior: Scholz, Jordan, Subotic, Westmann 2016 (Souffle); the Brie is Jordan et al.
organs.source_boundary: the RAM IR and index layer; CANDIDATE because only the file inventory was read

pressures.source_evidence: UnitTranslator.cpp semi-naive generation; the RAM and index inventory
pressures.condition: an organism computes the closure of recursive rules (e.g. reachability, points-to) over millions to billions of base facts; the score is time and peak memory; naive evaluation re-derives every tuple every round
pressures.resource_or_constraint: memory for the relations and their deltas; index structures
pressures.failure_condition: re-deriving tuples (naive evaluation's quadratic waste), holding expired relations, or a general index where a specialised one would fit
pressures.world_punishes: naive fixpoint; one index type for all relations; interpreting when speed is needed
pressures.world_rewards: semi-naive delta evaluation, SCC stratification with expiry, per-relation specialised indexes, optional compilation
pressures.observable_consequence: time and peak memory on a transitive-closure or points-to benchmark for naive vs semi-naive, and interpreted vs compiled, and general B-tree vs Brie indexes on dense relations
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: materialising the full closure by hand (the answer, not a method)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the least model must reproduce it; naive evaluation must show the re-derivation blowup on transitive closure; a single-index build must show the memory/time penalty on dense relations where the Brie wins: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: high-performance Datalog for program analysis (Scholz et al. 2016)
